Commentary.Commentary: We are back with the second innings to begin. The two Umpires are already out to the middle and the New Zealand players are seen in a huddle before spreading out to the field. It will be Neil Brand and Edward Moore to open the innings for South Africa. The Kiwi skipper Tim Southee is with the new ball and is all in readiness to begin the proceedings. Let's play...
...SECOND INNINGS...

New Zealand are all out on 511 after batting for 144 overs and 5 sessions. Kane Williamson's impressive 118 and Rachin Ravindra's exceptional 240 propelled New Zealand into a commanding position. Neil Brand, making his debut as the skipper, concluded the innings brilliantly with a remarkable 6-wicket haul for the Proteas. But the Kiwis will be delighted as they added some quickfire runs from Glenn Phillips, and Daryl Mitchell before getting all out. Matt Henry added 27 crucial runs to their tally at the backend and helped them breach the 500-run mark. South Africa will have to work really hard when they come out to bat and build partnerships as they have a huge total mounted ahead of them. Stay tuned as we bring the second innings just in a bit.

Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the final session on Day 2! The umpires are back out in the middle and so are the players of South Africa. Mitchell Santner and Kyle Jamieson are set to resume their stay on the crease as well. It will be the spin of Neil Brand to continue after the break. Let's play...
... Day 2, Session 3 ...

As for the Proteas, this was their best session so far with the ball, though they leaked runs simultaneously. Ruan de Swardt broke the partnership dismissing Williamson and also quickly got rid of Tom Blundell. Neil Brand the skipper, who bowled the least number of overs, ended up being the most successful bowler so far. He bowled a long spell and chipped in with three crucial wickets dismissing Daryl Mitchell, Glenn Phillips, and of course Rachin Ravindra. Just before half an hour or so of the Tea break, they spilled quick runs but would be delighted to see the back of Ravindra. They would aim to get the Kiwis all out quickly coming into the post-Tea session and also put some runs on the board before the day's end. Stay tuned for the crucial and final session of Day 2 which will commence just a few minutes from now.

TEA BREAK, DAY 2. SESSION SUMMARY - 27 Overs, 145 Runs, and 4 wickets. Finally, a fruitful and productive session for the Proteas as they dismissed Williamson, Mitchell, Blundell, and the double-centurion Rachin Ravindra. But the hosts will take it as they doubled the scoring rate in this session, thanks to Rachin Ravindra and Glenn Phillips' aggressive approach. New Zealand headed into the post-Lunch session with Williamson and Ravindra. Both scored runs without breaking a sweat before Williamson played an uncharacteristic shot and got out on 118. Daryl Mitchell stayed for a fair bit of time with Ravindra and stitched a quickfire 82-run stand but sooner departed on 34. Tom Blundell had a very brief stay at the crease but their intent was pretty clear to be aggressive as they got the runs on the board. Rachin Ravindra was stranded on 199 for a long time but eventually breached his first-ever double-century feat. His patience was well rewarded. Ravindra joined an elite group as the fourth Kiwi batsman to convert his maiden Test hundred into a double century. Meanwhile, Glenn Phillips wasted no time in getting off to a flying start, scoring 39 runs. Ravindra continued to boost the run rate with a series of boundaries, elevating the run rate until he departed with a well-accomplished 240, just before the break.
Pitched up on off stump, defended solidly off the front foot by Kyle Jamieson and that will be Tea on Day 2!

Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the post-Lunch session on Day 2! The umpires are back out in the middle and so are the players of South Africa. Rachin Ravindra and Daryl Mitchell are all set to resume their stay on the crease. It will be Ruan de Swardt to start proceedings after the interval. Let's go...
... Day 2, Session 2 ...

South Africa have been made to toil in the field for a Day and one session but only have three wickets to show for it. They bowled pretty well in the first session on Day 2 with Dane Paterson and Ruan de Swardt keeping things tight and they did induce a few false shots as well but to no avail. it was then Ruan de Swardt who did get a big breakthrough as the Proteas managed to hang onto a catch after dropping a few early in the game. The bowling changes didn't prove to be much effective and not many chances were created later in the session. South Africa need to find a way to pick up a few wickets on the trot as at the moment, it is very comfortable for the home side. Do join us at 6.10 am IST (12.40 am GMT) for a crucial post-Lunch session on Day 2.

SESSION SUMMARY - 28 overs, 72 runs and 1 wicket. End of another engrossing session of Test but at the Lunch interval on Day 2, New Zealand will be the much happier side. The hosts started the new day with two batters who had already notched up tons on Day 1 but they started watchfully. Neither Kane Williamson nor Rachin Ravindra could really score freely as the opposition bowlers kept things tight and after a while, Williamson played an uncharacteristic hoick and was caught out. Daryl Mitchell came in and looked positive at the start but went back in his shell soon enough before Rachin started to play a few shots and went past the 150-run mark. The Black Caps will now look to consolidate further but will look to score a bit more freely.
At the stumps on a fuller length, Daryl Mitchell leans on top of it and defends it. And it's time for Lunch on Day 2.

On the other hand, the South African pack entered the arena with six debutants. The bowlers showed promise. Tshepo Moreki debuted with a wicket off his first delivery to dismiss Devon Conway, while Dane Paterson claimed Tom Latham's wicket. Despite consistent pressure, they couldn't find breakthroughs. Breaking the Williamson-Ravindra partnership is crucial for them and would aim to get these two back in the hut as quickly as possible. Stay tuned as an exciting first session of Day 2 is just up!

Welcome back to Day 2 of the first Test match between New Zealand and South Africa at Bay Oval, Mount Maunganui! The hosts dominated Day 1, with Kane Williamson and Rachin Ravindra smashing unbeaten centuries, propelling the Kiwis to 258/2. Despite losing Devon Conway and Tom Latham early, Williamson and Ravindra made batting look effortless, showcasing solid defense and skillful stroke play. They each faced over 200 deliveries, with Williamson's elegant and conventional cover drives and Ravindra's confident display after being promoted up the order. With a strong batting lineup yet to come, New Zealand is in a commanding position, eyeing a formidable total.
...DAY 2, SESSION 1...

Right then, the first day ended up in the favor of the hosts and they would aim to build more from here coming into Day 2, considering the depth in their batting order. South Africa would aim to get quick wickets earlier in the first session tomorrow. That's all from our coverage for Day 1. Join us for the action on Day 2 on Monday at 3:30 am IST (10:00 pm GMT). Cheers, take care!

Throughout the day, South Africa's seamers worked tirelessly, creating opportunities with disciplined bowling but struggled to capitalize on them. Despite Duan Olivier and Tsepho Moreki generating pressure, the visitors failed to convert chances into wickets, compounded by dropped catches, which hindered their progress. Moreki made an impactful debut by claiming Conway with his first delivery, while Dane Paterson's dismissal of Latham showcased glimpses of their potential. However, the failure to capitalize on these moments allowed the Kiwi batsmen to navigate through challenging periods and steadily accumulate runs. Even opting for the new ball didn't yield any positive results and couldn't provide any inroads.

Earlier in the day, New Zealand were invited to bat and lost Devon Conway in the second over itself. Tom Latham couldn't capitalize on the start he got and perished on 20. But after that, it was all about these two stitching up a brilliant partnership of 219 runs, the third-highest third-wicket partnership for the Kiwis, from facing the swing and the seam earlier to batting till the end of the day. Williamson looked in extreme control as he hit some beautiful cover drives early on and was joined by Ravindra equally who, at first couldn't find any gaps but when he did, he didn't look back. They charged up against the pacers in the last half hour or so of the extended session and helped to post 258 on the board on the very first day.

This brings us to the end of an absorbing day 1 of this first Test and it's unarguably been New Zealand's day with Kane Williamson and Rachin Ravindra accelerating in this final session. Kane Williamson and Rachin Ravindra concluded the day's play unbeaten on 112 and 118, respectively, both playing over 200 deliveries each, showcasing patience, resilience and skill throughout the day. Despite surviving chances, both batsmen capitalized on loose deliveries, with Ravindra securing his maiden Test Century after being promoted up in the batting order. Kane Williamson too, breached the 100-run mark for the 30th time in his Test career. South Africa persisted with their pace attack, with Duan Olivier and Tsepho Moreki delivering extended spells, albeit without making breakthroughs. Neil Brand, the South African skipper and the only spinner of the pack, too, couldn't generate any breakthrough. Despite commendable ground fielding, the visitors dropped a couple of catches that proved costly.

New Zealand will be pretty pleased with the way things have panned out so far but in a time where we are seeing the scoring rate close to 4 runs in an over in Test matches, the Kiwis have chosen to remain watchful. Kane Williamson and Rachin Ravindra are putting on a big stand here and the former skipper has already notched up a half-century. They will be looking to finish Day 1 with as many wickets in hand as possible and pile on the pressure on Day 2. Join us in a few minutes as a crucial final session on Day 1 is coming up next.

SESSION SUMMARY - 27 overs, 60 runs and no wickets. Another fairly slow and sedate session for South Africa but they didn't bowl badly. The pacers actually bowled tight lines for most of the session and kept the scoring rate down but the major issue was the lack of wicket-taking being created. And, when the chance did come the catch was dropped which could be costly. They need to pick themselves up and show more intent when they come out after the interval if they are to make inroads late in the day.

Commentary.Commentary: We are back with the post-Lunch session to begin. The two Umpires have taken their positions and the Proteas fielders spread out to the field. Kane Williamson and Rachin Ravindra will resume their innings for the hosts. Tshepo Moreki (8-1-21-1) to lead the proceedings ahead with the ball. Let's play...
...DAY 1, Second Session...

For the Proteas, surprisingly they entered the arena with six debutants in their pack. They used four bowlers so far. But it didn't take too long for them to strike as Tsepho Moreki, on debut and in the very first over, dismissed Conway on a peach of a delivery and kept asking tough questions inviting the batters to find the nick. They persistently queried the Kiwi batters with questions, bowling on the channel outside off as the ball was getting good assistance. Dane Paterson came back to the attack, changing his end, and broke the brewing 37-run stand by dismissing Tom Latham, finding the conventional outside edge. Tsepho Moreki was pretty accurate with his lines and lengths and didn't bowl any loose deliveries allowing the batters to be at ease. The tourists would want to get these two out as quickly as possible in the second session. Do join us in the post-Lunch session which begins at 6.10 am IST (12.40 am GMT). Stay tuned.

LUNCH, DAY 1 - SESSION SUMMARY - 25 overs, 65 runs, and 2 wickets. This brings us to the end of the first session as the players head for Lunch on Day 1. It has been a sedate session if not at all. In pretty much of a shared session, New Zealand were invited to bat and were struck in the very second over as Devon Conway had a stay for a couple of balls before he fell wearing it on the pads. But after that, Kane Williamson and Tom Latham, both steadied the innings after an early loss. Williamson played some beautiful conventional drives, and he stands unbeaten at 26. Tom Latham was watchful in his approach as well, but perished the moment he looked well-settled. Rachin Ravindra, promoted at number 4, partnered Williamson well, helping the partnership to flourish. They would want to stitch the partnership as long as possible.
Good length over off stump, Kane Williamson stays solid in defense and that will be a maiden over. Also, the umpire call for Lunch on Day 1!

Commentary.Commentary: Done with the pre-match proceedings and it is now time to play. The umpires are out in the middle and the players of South Africa can be seen in a huddle before taking their places on the field. Six debutants for the Proteas in this game. It will be the left-handed duo of Tom Latham and Devon Conway to open the innings for New Zealand. Duanne Olivier has the new ball in hand and is raring to go. Let's play...

We are just a few minutes away from the start of the game but first the two sets of players line up for their respective national anthems. It will be the national anthem of South Africa first, followed by the national anthem of New Zealand.

South Africa (Playing XI) - Neil Brand (C), Edward Moore, Raynard van Tonder, Zubayr Hamza, David Bedingham, Keegan Petersen, Ruan de Swardt, Clyde Fortuin (WK), Duanne Olivier, Tshepo Moreki, Dane Paterson.
New Zealand (Playing XI) - Tom Latham, Devon Conway, Kane Williamson, Rachin Ravindra, Daryl Mitchell, Tom Blundell (WK), Glenn Phillips, Mitchell Santner, Kyle Jamieson, Matt Henry, Tim Southee (C).
TOSS - South Africa win the toss and they will BOWL first.

South Africa on the other hand will be fielding what one would call a 'second string' side for both Test matches as the high-profile players are fulfilling their franchise cricket commitments which is a topic that has been debated by cricket aficionados worldwide. Neil Brand will be leading the team and would be hoping that they pull off a shock. But will they be able to do so, that too on the Kiwis' hone turf? Only time will tell. Stay tuned as the toss and team updates aren't far away.

New Zealand enjoyed a fruitful T20I series against Pakistan not too long ago but they will now have to adjust a bit and get into the red-ball mode. Former skipper, Kane Williamson is back from the niggle he suffered early in that T20I series and the likes of Kyle Jamieson and Tom Blundell are also back from injuries. They will be eyeing a clean sweep against what is a particularly weakened Proteas side.

Hello and welcome to one and all. The excitement of Test cricket at the moment is quite riveting as we've witnessed a couple of stellar games in the last few days and now South Africa travel to New Zealand for a two-match Test series and the first game is about to get underway in sometime at Bay Oval in Mount Maunganui.
